Episode 212. Return Order (2)
Zed Runcandel. The only surviving figure among Siron's siblings.
He had headed to the Black Sea as soon as Rosa lost her mind and left the Sword Garden. He believed that Siron's return was the only way to reclaim the family from chaos.
That was already four years ago.
For four years, he had made his way through the Black Sea, even without a map. The expedition party facing Zed now knew better than anyone else how tremendous that was.
It was a nearly impossible feat.

After all, Zed's power was only at 8-star. Although his blessed physique of Runcandel made him comparable to a 10-star warrior, reaching the depths of the Black Sea was a stretch. It was something that even genuine 10-star warriors couldn't do.
But now, Zed was facing Siron.
Tears flowed from Luna as she recalled the many hardships and injustices Zed must have faced. The former Black Knights, who had been close to Zed for a long time, also felt their emotions surge.
Only Siron and Zed calmly met each other's eyes.
"It's been a long time, and you're calling me 'Lord'."
"I thought you might scold me for not using a proper title if I suddenly call you 'brother'. You often did that when we were young."
Siron recalled the times he scolded the young Zed and smiled slightly. After overcoming the demonic energy, Siron was smiling more often.
And Zed recognized Siron's change at a glance after seeing that.
"I should have scolded you less then. Seeing that you worry about that even at a moment like this."
"You've changed, brother. For the better."
"That's how it turned out."
Zed laughed heartily for a while and then wore a somber expression.
"Brother, the reason I came..."
"I know. It must be because of Rosa."
"...How did you know?"
"I met the youngest in my world. And he already knows about the calamity..."
Bitterness was evident in Siron's voice. Zed recognized the sadness embedded within that bitterness.

Siron, who had overcome his demonic nature, now had human emotions, unlike before. Of course, even without the demonic energy, his feelings weren't typical, having been steeped in blood and swords for such a long time. However, he clearly felt the sadness of losing his wife.
But as the head of the family, because of the sins committed by Rosa, and because he had left the family then and now, he could not afford to grieve.
"...You defeated the calamity?"
For Zed, the fact that Siron was grieving was less shocking than this news. After all, his reason for risking his life to come to the Black Sea was the calamity.
"You must have been wandering the Black Sea all this time, knowing nothing of the outside world."
"No, brother, you've been in the Black Sea far longer than I have."
"When you reach my state, you'll understand."
Jed was momentarily speechless, but then he nodded.
"Well… First, please explain in detail. Did our youngest brother really slay the demon? Then what happened to our family? Was there no need for me to come here?"
"It's true that our youngest brother slew the demon. I don't know what happened to our family afterwards. But if it's him, he must be leading well. And it was very good of you to come find me."
"Why is that?"

"You've become stronger. Even if a powerful enemy like a demon threatens our family again, many members of our family will rely on and support you. Even without hope, they will think of you. If it's Jed Runekendel, they think you can turn things around."
It was not just empty praise for his miraculous journey across the Black Sea.
Siron truly believed that Jed had accomplished that feat. And there's no one in the world who can judge another's abilities more accurately than Siron.
Jed had finally entered the realm of transcendence. And to Siron, he wasn't in the early stage, but had reached the mid stage.
"Ozudok."
[Yes, sir!]
"Prepare a meal. We must have a meal with my long-lost brother."

[Understood! Oh, earlier, when you passed me and Vanessa without a word, I wondered who you were, but it turns out you're the master's brother! Nice to meet you, I'm the monster Ozudok... You could say I'm in charge of the expedition's meals and am the funny guy.]
As Ozudok greeted him, he quickly carved a table out of the rocks of the Black Sea. Jed was able to guess how meals had been served in the Black Sea from Ozudok's familiar movements.

Even more shocking were the dishes that were placed on the table a moment later. After Ozudok had gathered remnants of chaos and monsters and Siron had purified them, they turned into large chunks of food. Ozudok expertly distributed the chunks on the table.
'It's amazing... Did everyone live off of eating just this?'
While Jed was amazed, the other members of the expedition greeted him.
"Uncle, it's great to see you in such an unexpected moment."
"Luna, you've gotten stronger, too. Seeing you makes me realize how far I still have to go."
"I feel the same way when I see my father."
"Really… well, that's comforting to hear…"
"Jed, you're probably the first to have come this far into the Black Sea on your own."
"Only because you and the expedition had cleared the way, Vanessa."
"Even so, what you achieved will remain a great feat in our family for a long time."
"Thank you, Tuven. I remember the days when I used to make a fuss about defeating you. Same goes for Heijin over there."
While the cheerful exchanges continued, the meal preparation was completed. As Siron was about to take a bite, Jed took something out of his pocket.
"Oh, oh! Jed, what is that!?"
"Uncle! This is...!"
It was food.

A few handfuls of preserved grains and herbs that he had saved till the very end. For the expedition, who had been eating only purified chaos and monsters for the past few years, it was wholesome food they hadn't seen in a long time.
If the expedition hadn't already dealt with the Black Sea's kings like Kial and Sue, and the ruling monster-like entities in each area of the Black Sea, that food would have all gone bad.
Seeing the expedition members' eyes light up at the sight of the food, Jed sighed inwardly with a pitiful heart.
The first to reach for the food was Siron. He picked only one grain of each type, and selected only a small root or leaf piece from the herbs.
"I'm good with this. You guys divide the rest evenly and eat."
"I'll pass too, brother. I ate a lot on the way here."
"I see. Ah, Luna. You should pass too."
"Yes, father... What? Me? Why...?"
"Now you're answering back, you find this old man amusing, huh?"
"Hup, understood."
"Vanessa."
"Yes, master. Oh, don't tell me I...?"
"Yes. And Tuven."
"Understood."
"Heijin. You too."
"Yes, master."
Jed, Luna, Vanessa, Tuven, Heijin.
Ozudok thus divided the food among all except these five. It was a perfect division, down to a single grain.
A human-like meal began after a long time. The ones who didn't receive any food had the usual meal.
Munching sounds.
For a while, the sound of chewing and swallowing continued. The expedition members found the starchy taste of the grains and the bitter taste of the herbs to be as sweet as sugar.
"Why do you think I excluded you five?"
"I don't know, father."

"I too, like you, was strong from the time I was young, so I didn't have much experience understanding the intentions of others, but you're a bit too much. When you return, learn what tact is from our youngest, Luna."
"Yes, I under... Wait, did you say 'when I return'?"
The pupils of Luna and the Black Knight expedition members grew larger. Ozudok was surprised enough to drop his jaw.
[Cough, cough. Oh... the bitterness of the herbs becomes richer with the taste of phlegm. Ha, haha. Anyway, returning? Are Luna and the other knights... leaving the Black Sea now!?]
Siron nodded. Those who had received the command to return stared at him, calming their surprised hearts.
"When you return, you'll eat better foods, so it's right to give all the food Jed brought to the others here."
"Father. We cannot leave this heavy burden only to you and the others and depart."
"I told you to pick up on social cues, not talk back."
"But father!"
When Luna stood up and shouted, the other knights were taken aback. No matter if it was Luna, it was something that shouldn't have happened to show such a sight to Siron.
However, Siron gestured to the knights who were trying to calm Luna down that it was okay.
"Luna, you're probably worried about me and the other knights."
"Even if you have overcome the devil, we all have seen it. It's too dangerous without us, even if you're our father. So please reconsider the order, father."
"Luna. If you think that I am preparing for the future in case the expedition is wiped out, you're wrong. I also have no intention of perishing with the remaining kings of the Black Sea."
I will kill all the kings of the Black Sea and return to the clan.
Siron continued in that way and met Luna's eyes.

"If I had even a little bit of the same thoughts as you, I would have entrusted the Barisada to you right here and now. It's a message to be delivered to the youngest. But I will keep the Barisada. Because I don't plan to die in the Black Sea. Honestly, I didn't have that feeling before, but now I don't at all."
"Then shouldn't we have even more reason not to return? The quicker we deal with all the kings of the Black Sea and return together..."
"It's because the situation is more dangerous there than here right now."
"The youngest's place... Are you saying it's more dangerous than here?"

"Relatively speaking, yes. The clan doesn't currently have me. Powerful enemies are awakening in the insects. Already, a magician too strong to comprehend has appeared in Jiplen, and not on the ground. From somewhere I've never been, unknown beings are revealing their power."
It couldn't be a fabricated story. The senses of Siron that the expedition had seen so far were reaching a level not lacking to be called a god, not a demi-god.
"So, you should return and help the youngest. Also, from this time on, I formally appoint him as my successor, the small family head."
Those who received the return order bowed their heads together.

"I'll open the way for you to return more easily after the meal. I'll need some time because I have to spread all my energy across the Black Sea for a while. Until then, we can share some backlogged stories."
"...Understood, father. We'll be waiting to help the youngest when we return."
"Jed."
"Speak, brother."
Shiron momentarily raised his head to gaze at the dark sky of the Black Sea and then added these words:
"When you return, convey this message to the youngest. Tell them, 'I'm sorry it was you, not me, who had to slay the evil spirit.'"
